history.alt_text: A heavy unbranded workstation graphics card resting on a dark studio surface.
history.caption: The shift toward massive memory arrays is rewriting the economics of compute hardware.
history.title: workstation-gpu-memory-pricing

style_when: the story is a product, a device, a price or a market for a thing the reader could buy — an appliance, a panel, a router, a robot arm
prompt: Studio product photograph, 85mm prime lens with crisp focal depth, asymmetrical three-quarter view with heavy off-centre framing. A massive, unbranded professional workstation graphics card featuring heavy brushed aluminum cooling fins and prominently exposed black memory silicon banks. The premium hardware rests heavily on a dark, textured slate studio surface. A single softbox key light throws a long, deep contact shadow across the stone, highlighting the precise metallic edges and matte polymer shrouds. Clean, high-contrast atmosphere, muted sophisticated color palette, generous editorial negative space on the left side, catalogue clarity.
negative_prompt: text, typography, letters, numbers, watermarks, garbled UI, logos
rationale: The story revolves around a physical product (a graphics card) and its market pricing shift from consumer to professional tiers. A premium studio object shot emphasizes the physical hardware and its high-end price tag.
subject: A heavy, unbranded professional workstation graphics card with exposed memory banks
core_thesis: Compute pricing is now entirely dictated by memory capacity, as seen in the withdrawal of consumer 32GB cards in favor of expensive 84GB professional hardware.
core_conflict: Consumer affordability vs. enterprise memory pricing power
composition: asymmetrical three-quarter view with heavy off-centre framing
alt_text: The GPU Memory Squeeze. A heavy unbranded workstation graphics card resting on a dark studio surface.
caption: The GPU Memory Squeeze: Compute is now priced by memory space, not raw speed.
title: The GPU Memory Squeeze
